sources.name: PAPSS: Pan-African Payment and Settlement System
CBN Foreign Exchange Manual (Trade and Exchange Department), revised edition, March 2018

entries.subject: pta_quarterly_limit
entries.display: Personal Travel Allowance is capped at US$4,000 per quarter
entries.quote: The allowable limit for Personal Travel Allowance (PTA) and Business Travel Allowance (BTA) is US$4,000.00 and US$5,000.00 per quarter, respectively.
entries.notes: PTA of US$4,000 per quarter is restated unchanged in the 4th Edition (2026), Memorandum 8.

entries.subject: bta_quarterly_limit
entries.display: Business Travel Allowance is capped at US$5,000 per quarter
entries.quote: The allowable limit for Personal Travel Allowance (PTA) and Business Travel Allowance (BTA) is US$4,000.00 and US$5,000.00 per quarter, respectively.
entries.notes: The 2018 revision states a US$5,000 quarterly BTA. The 4th Edition (2026) does not restate a BTA figure, so this may no longer hold; treat as historical.

entries.subject: pta_eligible_age
entries.display: Only persons aged 18 and above may buy Personal Travel Allowance
entries.quote: Only persons, 18 years old and above are qualified to purchase PTA.

entries.subject: bta_pta_exclusivity
entries.display: A traveller entitled to BTA cannot also claim PTA for the same trip, and vice versa
entries.quote: travelers on business trip who are entitled to BTA shall not be eligible for PTA while on the same trip or vice versa

entries.subject: medical_travel_allowance_limit
entries.display: Authorised buyers may sell a medical travel allowance of up to US$5,000 per transaction
entries.quote: Authorised buyers can sell medical travel allowance subject to a limit of USS85, 000.00 per transaction
entries.notes: OCR renders US$5,000.00 as 'USS85, 000.00'; the cleaned reading is US$5,000.00.

entries.subject: domiciliary_source_of_funds
entries.display: A customer opening or funding a domiciliary account need not disclose the source of funds
entries.quote: shall not be required or obliged to disclose the source of funds to be deposited in such account

entries.subject: domiciliary_cash_withdrawal_rule
entries.display: Where more than US$10,000 in cash was imported and deposited, withdrawals from the domiciliary account must be in cash only
entries.quote: Where a person imports foreign currency in excess of $10,000 00 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies, In cash and deposits same in the Domiciliary Account, withdrawal from the account shall be in cash only.

entries.subject: papss_settlement_currency
entries.value_text: local currencies of originator and beneficiary, no pre-funding in hard currency
entries.display: PAPSS pays the beneficiary in their local currency and settles intra-African payments without converting through a third currency
entries.quote: Instant payments made by originators to beneficiaries in their local currencies, no matter where they are in Africa

entries.subject: papss_definition
entries.value_text: cross-border financial market infrastructure for payments across Africa
entries.display: PAPSS is a cross-border financial market infrastructure enabling payment transactions across Africa
entries.quote: PAPSS – the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System – is a cross-border, financial market infrastructure enabling payment transactions across Africa.

entries.subject: pta_disbursement_split
entries.display: At least 75% of PTA must be disbursed via cards and approved digital channels, the remaining 25% in cash
entries.quote: The disbursement of PTA shall be a minimum of 75% via cards and other approved digital channels, while the remaining 25% shall be paid in cash.
entries.notes: 4th Edition is undated on its cover; effective_from is the CBN launch date of 15 May 2026.

entries.subject: family_maintenance_remittance
entries.display: A resident may remit up to 100% of net income for dependants, once a month
entries.quote: are allowed up to 100% of their net income while physically resident in Nigeria. PHR is restricted to net income credited to the bank account.
entries.notes: Same page: actual transfer may be made once a month, based on the previous month's remuneration. Quote starts mid-sentence because the preceding line is hyphenated in the PDF.

entries.subject: ecci_issuance_deadline
entries.display: An e-CCI must be issued within 24 hours of converting capital inflows to naira
entries.quote: An electronic Certificate of Capital Importation (e-CCI) MUST be issued for all capital transfers into Nigeria, within 24 hours of the conversion of funds into Naira by an Authorised Dealer Bank.

entries.subject: export_repatriation_non_oil
entries.display: Non-oil export proceeds must reach the exporter's domiciliary account within 180 days of shipment
entries.quote: payment for the shipment is credited to the exporter’s Domiciliary Account within the stipulated period of one hundred and eighty (180) days from the date of shipment.
entries.notes: Same section: Form NXP is valid 180 days; one 90-day extension may be approved by the bank.

entries.subject: export_repatriation_oil_gas
entries.display: Oil and gas export proceeds must reach the exporter's domiciliary account within 90 days of shipment
entries.quote: credited to the exporters’ Domiciliary Account in Nigeria within the stipulated period of ninety (90) days from the date of shipment of the goods.

entries.subject: ness_levy_oil_gas
entries.display: NESS levy on crude oil and gas exports is 0.12% of FOB value
entries.quote: the Nigerian Export Supervision Scheme (NESS) Levy, which is currently 0.12% of the F.O.B value of the exported crude oil/gas and related products.

notes: Two CBN FX manuals are cited. The March 2018 revision (file renamed from cbn_fx_manual_2026.pdf to cbn_fx_manual_2018_rev.pdf after its cover showed the real date) supports PTA/BTA, age and domiciliary rules. The 4th Edition (launched 15 May 2026) supports the PTA disbursement split, e-CCI deadline, family maintenance, export repatriation and NESS levy. Where they overlap the 4th Edition wins. USD amounts are in USD_cents.
